label: first copy-phase input (re-fed first token) in length-9 sequences starting with n/y/w/2/j/z/k
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit that fires only at one position: the step right after <DEL>, where the model reads its first output (original token 0) back in and outputs original token 1 (recall_idx == 1). Nearly all of it (98% of mass) is in L = 9 sequences (t = 10); a handful fire at L = 8. It never fires in the original or delimiter phases or at any later copy step. Which first token is re-fed matters a lot: n alone is half the mass and has the largest activations, then y, w, 2, j, with weaker z and k; other first tokens almost never fire. Within that context it is still selective: only about 10% of qualifying steps (and about 29% for first token n) cross the threshold, and I found no simple variable (second token, digit count, repeats) that separates them, so precision is low. Recall and mass recall are about 0.97-0.98.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=n (+5.03), t=10 & in_tok=y (+3.57), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=w (+3.28), t=10 & in_tok=j (+2.67), t=10 & in_tok=2 (+1.81), recall_idx=1 & in_tok=2 (+1.80). Lower it: orig1=v (-1.88), orig6=1 (-1.86), orig2=f (-1.77), orig7=- (-1.66).
